emily: Opening a quick thread for a docs PR that covers RHEL/CentOS packaging and an offline bundle variant. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4621. Main changes: add .rpm packaging instructions, explain difference when selinux/enforcing is on, and a troubleshooting note about firewalld vs nftables when installing in constrained private networks. PTAL.

rafael: Thanks. Can we be explicit about how to build the offline bundle on RHEL7 vs RHEL8+? RHEL7 uses init/systemd hybrid and may not have nftables. Suggest callouts: `yum install --downloadonly` flow and how to vendor rpms into the tarball.

priya: Added a short example for vendoring rpms: 

```bash
# on builder host (RHEL8+ recommended)
mkdir -p /tmp/offline-rpms
repoquery --resolve --alldeps --download-path=/tmp/offline-rpms redwood-installer
cp /tmp/offline-rpms/*.rpm ./airgap-bundle/
```

priya: Also included a note to verify package signatures offline: `rpm --checksig --nosignature *.rpm` and how to add the vendor GPG key into the tarball and import with `rpm --import <vendor.pub>` before installation.

nora: For networking docs, please add a short troubleshooting section: we saw a customer where firewalld zones blocked the installer preflight probes even though nftables rules looked fine. Proposed troubleshooting steps:

1) Check firewalld runtime vs permanent: `firewall-cmd --list-all --zone=public`
2) If using nftables rules directly, ensure firewalld is disabled or the rules are added via `firewall-cmd --direct` so they persist across reloads
3) Quick probe command: `curl -sS --connect-timeout 3 http://127.0.0.1:8080/health` from installer host after enabling verbose logs

nora: Also added a tiny systemd tmpfile suggestion for constrained systems that don't persist /var/lib/redwood across reboots:

```ini
# /etc/tmpfiles.d/redwood.conf
D /var/lib/redwood 0755 redwood redwood -
```

emily: Good catches. One more: include a Go SDK example showing mTLS client certs when the customer's egress appliance terminates outbound TLS but requires mutual auth to the appliance. I added a short snippet: 

```go
// Go example: custom http.Transport with client cert for mTLS to egress appliance
package main
import (
  "crypto/tls"
  "crypto/x509"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
)
func main() {
  cert, _ := tls.LoadX509KeyPair("/etc/redwood/certs/client.crt", "/etc/redwood/certs/client.key")
  caCert, _ := ioutil.ReadFile("/etc/redwood/certs/egress-ca.crt")
  caPool := x509.NewCertPool()
  caPool.AppendCertsFromPEM(caCert)

  tr := &http.Transport{
    TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{
      RootCAs:      caPool,
      Certificates: []tls.Certificate{cert},
    },
  }
  client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
  resp, err := client.Get("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health")
  if err != nil { panic(err) }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
}
```

rafael: LGTM for the Go snippet. Suggest callout: when appliance does TLS termination, you may need to set `InsecureSkipVerify=false` and ensure the CA chain is present. Also add note about rotating client certs via the regular secrets rotation runbook (link to /docs/runbooks/secrets-rotation.md).

priya: I added a small section about SELinux: commands to label the installer directories if SELinux is enforcing: `semanage fcontext -a -t var_lib_t '/var/lib/redwood(/.*)?' && restorecon -Rv /var/lib/redwood`.

emily: CI passed for PR #4621 (:white_check_mark:). I'll land after a quick editorial pass. Thanks for the quick reviews.
